script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

INT. A LITTLE COFFEE SHOP - DAY

A quiet little coffee shop in the heart of the city. The smell of freshly brewed coffee permeates the air. SARAH (30s), a barista, is making a cappuccino for a CUSTOMER.

CUSTOMER
(to Sarah)
You're always so kind, Sarah.

SARAH
(smiling)
Thank you, sir. It's my pleasure to serve you.

As Sarah hands the customer his drink, ANNA (early 30s), Sarah's estranged sister, walks in. Sarah's face falls.

---

INT. A LITTLE COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Sarah's heart races as she watches Anna approach the counter. Their eyes meet, and for a moment, they're both frozen in time.

ANNA
(with a hint of sadness)
Can I have a latte, please?

Sarah's hands tremble as she makes Anna's drink.

---

INT. A LITTLE COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Sarah hands Anna her drink, but their eyes are locked in a silent confrontation.

SARAH
(sternly)
Why are you here, Anna?

ANNA
(tearfully)
I've come to ask for your forgiveness.

---

EXT. CITY PARK - DAY

A beautiful day in the park, and Sarah and Anna sit on a bench, facing each other.

ANNA
(voice shaking)
I know I hurt you, Sarah. I know I made mistakes, but I can't change the past. All I can do is ask for your forgiveness and try to make things right.

SARAH
(angrily)
What makes you think I'll even consider it? You abandoned me when I needed you the most.

ANNA
(tearfully)
I was young and selfish, Sarah. I made a mistake, and I've paid for it ever since. But I've grown, and I've changed. I've missed you, and I want to be a part of your life again.

---

EXT. CITY PARK - DAY

Sarah looks at Anna, her sister, with a mixture of anger and sadness.

SARAH
(sighing)
I don't know, Anna. I can't just forget what you did.

ANNA
(placing a hand on Sarah's)
I understand, Sarah. But if you give me a chance, I promise I'll make it up to you. I'll be there for you, no matter what.

---

INT. A LITTLE COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Sarah is behind the counter, making a drink for a customer. Anna walks in, and Sarah hesitates before greeting her.

ANNA
(smiling)
Good morning, Sarah.

Sarah looks up, and for the first time in years, she smiles back.

SARAH
(warmly)
Morning, Anna.

---

EXT. CITY STREET - DAY

Sarah and Anna walk down the street, arm in arm. They've reconciled, and their bond is stronger than ever.

ANNA
(whispering in Sarah's ear)
Thank you for giving me another chance, Sarah.

SARAH
(smiling)
Anytime, Anna. Family is forever.

FADE OUT.
---

End of screenplay.
